subject: NewYear burst SLO carveout & conditional fallback — hosted API (p50/p95)
messages:
From: Ava Collins <ops@cedarline.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cedarline.health>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@cedarline.health>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Request: temporary p95 carveout for New Year promo spike

Diego,

Quick context: Cedarline has a marketing promotion scheduled for 2027-01-01 that historically drives a large spike in API traffic for our patient-summary feature. Our engineering/ops team ran a forecast and we expect a 3-4x token/req volume spike concentrated in a 36–48 hour window starting 2026-12-31 23:00 UTC. Forecast attached (cedarline_q4_promo_forecast.csv).

We need Redwood's help to avoid user-facing timeouts during the surge. Specifically we're asking for either: 1) a temporary adjustment to the hosted API p95 latency commitment for the US region for the 48-hour window, or 2) a contractual carveout/derating so we don't trigger SLA credits while we absorb the burst.

As part of the request, we can provide additional telemetry and will accept increased monitoring hooks. We're hoping for an outcome that keeps production traffic online without formal Dedicated capacity right now.

Can you confirm what temporary tolerances Redwood can offer, how you'd measure the window, and what evidence you need from us (PO, forecast, runbook) to finalize an amendment?

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Ops Lead, Cedarline Health
ops@cedarline.health
(Attachment: cedarline_q4_promo_forecast.csv)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ops@cedarline.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 carveout for New Year promo spike

Hi Ava — thanks for the heads-up and the forecast. Appreciate you sharing the data.

High-level proposal from Redwood (one-time temporary amendment):
- Window: 2026-12-31 23:00 UTC through 2027-01-02 23:00 UTC (48 hours) for US region (primary traffic: us-east).
- p50/p95 commitments during window: p50 unchanged; p95 nominal target relaxed from 300ms -> 450ms for the window only.
- Measurement: rolling 60-minute windows, standard token-weighted sampling (we'll provide sample IDs). Carveout applies to p95 breaches measured within the defined window only.
- Safeguard: if elevated p95 persists >72 hours after start (indicating sustained capacity pressure), Redwood will trigger the agreed fallback: either accelerate Dedicated provisioning for your reserved pool or invoke routing to a quantized model variant; we will notify you and share remediation ETA.
- Evidence required to finalize amendment: signed PO (PDF), a 1-page runbook (ops contacts + monitoring channel), and permission to attach a monitoring webhook to your ops channel.

I've attached a draft amendment (rdw-proposed-carveout-amendment-v1.pdf) that captures the above language and the precise measurement clauses. Marissa, could you confirm the phrasing around measurement buckets and sampling is operationally accurate? Ben, I'll need procurement support on accepted billing/crediting approach if the carveout is used.

If Cedarline agrees to the window above, we can prepare a DocuSign amendment and aim to have it signed before the start time.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
(Attachment: rdw-proposed-carveout-amendment-v1.pdf)

Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 carveout for New Year promo spike

Ava / Diego — added a few operational clarifications from SRE/product side to make sure the amendment is unambiguous: 

1) Measurement details:
   - We will compute p50/p95 on token-weighted request latencies, aggregated in 60-minute rolling windows.
   - For the carveout to apply, p95 must exceed the relaxed threshold in at least 12 non-overlapping 60-minute windows during the 48-hour window (this prevents brief microbursts from consuming the carveout).
   - Transient overload mitigations (prefetch/batching reductions) will be excluded from p95 samples (standard practice) — we will provide the exact sampling SQL.

2) Region & model variants:
   - The carveout will be scoped to your primary region (us-east). Traffic routed to EU or APAC endpoints will be measured under their normal commitments.
   - If sustained >72 hours, we will route new traffic to a quantized-compatible variant (lower-cost/better throughput) unless you request Dedicated capacity. We'll provide a compatibility checklist for your request.

3) Monitoring & hooks:
   - We'll add an ops webhook and a temporary read-only SLO dashboard to your shared folder. Please confirm the Slack channel for high-priority alerts (we suggest #cedarline-ops).

4) Operational runbook ask from your side:
   - Single-page runbook with primary/backup contacts and an approved escalation path to accept short-term model fallback.

Diego — language in the amendment needs to reflect the "12-window rule" and the fallback activation criteria. I've added comments to rdw-proposed-carveout-amendment-v1.pdf.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
